reason: The developing red cells need haemoglobin to carry oxygen, and the supplied materials are its building blocks.
expectation: The cells will make haemoglobin as they develop.

effect: The developing cells assembled haemoglobin and matured into nucleus-free red blood cells; the blood sample still needs its fluid components.
reaction: The cutaway usefully distinguishes haemoglobin production in developing cells from the mature cells.
reason: Water and dissolved solutes are the visible components of plasma.
expectation: They will form plasma for the blood sample.

effect: Water and solutes formed plasma, ready to receive the blood cells.
reaction: The straw-yellow plasma makes the fluid component distinct from the cells.
reason: Red blood cells suspended in plasma are a natural next step toward the blood sample.
expectation: The red cells will join the plasma to form a partial blood sample.

effect: The red cells had to bind oxygen before joining plasma; they are now oxygen-bearing carriers.
reaction: The automatic combination clarified the required order, and the reversible binding diagram connects oxygen uptake with release.
reason: The oxygen-bearing red cells and plasma are the main components of the sample.
expectation: The oxygen-bearing cells will be suspended in plasma.

effect: The oxygen-bearing red cells are now suspended in plasma, but white cells and platelets are still absent.
reaction: The partial-sample picture makes the missing components clear.
reason: Adding the remaining white cells and platelets should complete the blood sample.
expectation: The white cells and platelets will join the oxygen-bearing red cells in plasma.

effect: Adding white cells and platelets completed the blood sample and the chapter goal.
reaction: The final picture plan clearly distinguishes the blood components, though it says little about what white cells and platelets do.

mostWorthwhile.text: The oxygen-binding result was most worthwhile: its reversible arrow and explanation connect haemoglobin to oxygen release in working tissues.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final assembly was predictable, and the white cells and platelets remain largely unexplained despite appearing in the completed sample.

surprise.text: I expected red cells to join plasma directly, but the attempt instead automatically combined them with oxygen. The result also showed oxygen binding and release as reversible.

arbitrary.text: Requiring oxygen to bind before red cells could be added to plasma felt like a game-ordering constraint rather than an explained biological necessity.

continue.text: I would continue: the planned illustrations connect structure to function clearly, and I would be curious to see how circulation brings oxygen carriers near tissues. The straightforward assembly steps alone were less engaging.
